the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Musashi Province]].

== History ==
Its founding date is unknown. However, it is said to be the origin of the "miya" in the local place name {{ill|Miyaharachō|ja|宮原町 (さいたま市)|qid=Q11453414|lt=Miyahara-ch?}}<ref>For details, see {{ill|Miyahara|ja|宮原村 (埼玉県)|ko|미야하라촌 (사이타마현)|qid=Q11453404|lt=Miyahara Village}} and {{ill|Miyaharachō|ja|宮原町 (さいたま市)|qid=Q11453414|lt=Miyahara-ch?}}.</ref>, and to have been founded by inviting a divided spirit from {{ill|Kamigamo Shrine|Q700448|qid=Q700448}} of {{ill|Yamashiro Province|Q749276|qid=Q749276}} Ichinomiya. {{ill|Kissh?in|ja|吉祥院 (さいたま市北区)|qid=Q124483193|lt=Kissh?in}} in the same ward served as its {{ill|Bettō-ji|ja|別当寺|qid=Q11396755}}<ref name="??">Saitama Prefecture Shrine Office Shrine Survey Group (ed.), ''Shrines of Saitama: Kita-Adachi, Kodama, Minami-Saitama'', Saitama Prefecture Shrine Office, 1998, pp. 224-225</ref>.

In {{ill|1873|Q7757|qid=Q7757}} (Meiji 6), it was ranked as a village shrine under the {{ill|Q712534|lt=Modern shrine ranking system}}, and during shrine mergers in the late Meiji period, surrounding shrines were merged into it. In {{ill|1919|Q2157|qid=Q2157}} (Taish? 8), the worship hall burned down<ref name="??"></ref>.

== Access ==
* 8 minutes on foot from {{ill|Miyahara Station|Q845070|qid=Q845070}}.
